clue.text: Stupid sort of crossword that's impossible

definitions.meaning: lacking any idea or understanding, dim
a puzzle printed without its hints could never be solved

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a crossword is stupid and impossible.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean without a clue: a dim person has none, and a puzzle with none printed cannot be done.

clue.text: Cook numbers written in code

indicators.note: the numbers are set down inside the word for code, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as the word itself
DL is 550 in Roman numerals, a pair of numbers

explanation.surface: A cook writes recipe quantities in secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals supply the numbers: D is 500 and L is 50.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle eggs is to cook them gently in water just below boiling.

clue.text: Like the best team without a fixture?

definitions.meaning: having no equal, beaten by none
having no match arranged against an opponent

explanation.surface: A top sports team finds itself with no game scheduled.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrivalled teams have no equal; a team with no fixture has no game or match booked.

clue.text: Boy gets up around one, having enjoyed this!

definitions.text: Boy gets up around one, having enjoyed this!

indicators.note: the turned name goes round the letter for one, holding it inside
in a down clue the boy's name rises, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Neil is a boy's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boy finally rises late in the day after a long, pleasant sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' turns NEIL into LIEN; 'around' puts I inside it after the E. The whole clue also describes the scene: a lad gets up late after his lazy morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A late morning in bed, the treat that makes someone rise around one o'clock.

clue.text: Capital protection from St Neots

indicators.note: the hat is made from the letters of the town's name, rearranged

parts.note: a market town in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: A hat bought in the English town of St Neots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is a pun on caput, the head: the definition means headgear. ST NEOTS is a small town in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's wide-brimmed hat, which shields the head, here punningly called the capital.

clue.text: Also a dandy

parts.note: a swell is an old word for a fashionable, smartly dressed man

explanation.surface: A dandy turns up too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in addition, besides, too.

clue.text: It's painfully obvious

parts.note: an aching digit that sticks out, from the idiom about something that stands out awkwardly

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that something is blindingly obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom to stick out like this, said of something conspicuous; the injured digit literally hurts.

clue.text: Girl found on the moors

definitions.meaning: the botanical genus of heath plants growing on open moorland

explanation.surface: A girl is discovered out on the moors.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, and the Latin genus name for heather, which carpets upland moors.

clue.text: Educated elite wrong to admit strike breaker

indicators.note: the rearranged letters let the strike breaker in, holding it inside
the letters of elite are set wrong, that is rearranged

parts.note: a rat is slang for a worker who breaks a strike, a scab

explanation.surface: An educated elite wrongly lets a scab into their circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ELITE as LITEE before 'to admit' takes in the strike breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to read and write, and so schooled or well read.

clue.text: Directions enclosed with fire control — a wet blanket!

indicators.note: the two compass points are shut inside the word for the fire control

parts.note: a damper is a plate in a flue that regulates a fire's draught
E and N are the compass points east and north

explanation.surface: Firefighting instructions close with a soaked blanket thrown over the flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wet blanket' looks literal next to fire control, but it means a killjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both name something or someone that spoils enthusiasm or fun.

clue.text: Sun god, apparently, follows a successful one

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Sun god, apparently, follows a successful one' (6) for ARTIST: no parse found giving A, R, T, I, S, T from these words, and no blog or database gives it; possibly an OCR misreading.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sun god, apparently, follows a successful one

clue.text: Stiff sort of language

definitions.meaning: the kind of language expressed by gesture and posture

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a stilted, stiff style of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff is slang for a corpse; posture and gesture make up non-verbal communication of that name.

clue.text: You don't speak it? The French can!

parts.note: la is the feminine word for the in French
a tin is a can, as of food

explanation.surface: A taunt that the French can speak a language when you cannot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a dead language, one nobody speaks any more.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Roman tongue is no longer spoken anywhere as a native language.

clue.text: What marines have that's like a cat

definitions.meaning: a breed of domestic cat, as in British or American varieties

explanation.surface: Something marines possess that also resembles a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Marines wear their hair cropped, and British and American breeds of domestic cat carry the same name.

clue.text: Outlaw takes shelter in a mountain Kingdom

indicators.note: the outlaw word takes the shelter in, holding it inside

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
a hut is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: A bandit hides out in a remote Himalayan realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun but is the verb; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Buddhist monarchy in the eastern Himalayas.

clue.text: Where food may be found in the bush

definitions.text: Where food may be found in the bush

parts.words: Where food may be found in the bush
parts.note: in Australian slang tucker is food, and a bushman carries his provisions in a sack of that name

explanation.surface: Asking where provisions might be kept in the Australian outback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bush' is the Australian outback, not a shrub; tucker is Australian slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian traveller's sack for carrying provisions in the outback.

clue.text: Order to be patient sounds threatening

definitions.meaning: a command to hold on a moment
said menacingly it promises revenge later

explanation.surface: An instruction to be patient that carries a menacing tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an instruction to hold on and a menacing promise of comeuppance, as in 'just wait and see'.

clue.text: Cook roast duck, say, for Armstrong?

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or alter, so the letters of roast are rearranged
say signals that the word for duck is heard, not spelt

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of zero, a nought

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to roast a duck, served to someone called Armstrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' turns ROAST into ASTRO. NOUGHT spoken sounds like NAUT. A duck is a zero score in cricket. Neil Armstrong was the first man on the moon; the question mark marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong is the most famous space traveller, the first to walk on the moon.

clue.text: It may seem excessive in a churchwarden

definitions.text: It may seem excessive in a churchwarden

parts.words: It may seem excessive in a churchwarden
parts.note: a churchwarden is also a long clay tobacco pipe, whose shank looks absurdly long

explanation.surface: Something about a parish official seems a bit much.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is a clay pipe with a very long shank, not only a parish officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The shank of a tobacco pipe, extremely long in the churchwarden type.

clue.text: Signs of power cuts at home, initially

indicators.note: the at-home word comes first in the answer although it follows in the clue

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
dices means cuts into small cubes

explanation.surface: Power cuts at home are the first signs of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signs of power' are mathematical exponents. 'initially' moves IN to the front of DICES.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra, exponents showing how many times a quantity is multiplied by itself.

clue.text: The location of sense, so to speak

indicators.note: signals that the word for a sense is heard aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A musing about where the senses reside.
explanation.definitionFit: A place or position where something is situated.

clue.text: Copper coins once used in measurement

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
bits are coins, such as the old threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Copper coins that were once used to measure out goods.
explanation.walkthrough: BITS are coins, as in the old British threepenny bit.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient measure of length, roughly a forearm long, used in biblical times.

clue.text: Miner's dog seen on end of pier

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word pier is taken

explanation.surface: A miner's dog is spotted at the far end of a pier.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Miner's' is a link, has.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal worker who digs underground.

clue.text: Work out a maths problem concerning air supply

indicators.note: the letters are worked out, that is reshuffled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Solving a maths problem about the supply of air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' rearranges MATHS as STHMA. 'problem' looks like part of the maths task but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A respiratory condition that makes breathing difficult.

clue.text: Basic compound of tin, for instance, and aluminium

parts.note: tin is an example of a chemical element
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A simple chemical compound made of tin and aluminium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound of' is a link, saying the answer is made of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamental, primary, concerned with first principles.

clue.text: Headless monster could be a howler

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is cut off the word for monster

parts.note: a terror is a frightening creature or an unruly child

explanation.surface: A headless monster that could be a howling beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless' removes the T from TERROR. 'howler' suggests a wailing creature but means a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A howler is a glaring blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Vote for the end of supertax?

definitions.meaning: the mark made on a ballot paper
the last letter of supertax is an X, which is that shape

explanation.surface: A vote for abolishing the higher-rate tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters mark their choice with an X, and supertax ends in that same saltire shape.

clue.text: Doctor cared for key personnel

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of cared are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor looked after the most important staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A core group of trained people at the heart of an organisation.

clue.text: Bothers about losing English pounds

indicators.note: about means around or in a muddle, so the letters are rearranged
one letter of the fodder goes missing before the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is bothered about losing English money.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E out of BOTHERS ('losing English') to leave BOTHRS, which 'about' rearranges. 'pounds' looks like money but is the verb, beats.
explanation.definitionFit: Beats heavily and rhythmically, as a heart or a headache does.

clue.text: Garden feature with bad design in Genesis

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for genesis

parts.note: genesis means origin or beginning, a birth

indicators.note: the letters of bad are put into a new design, rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly designed garden ornament from the Book of Genesis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges BAD as DBA. Genesis here means a beginning, not the Bible book.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow basin set in a garden for birds to drink and wash in.

clue.text: Road rage regarded as an illusion

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its digit read as a letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Road rage seen as a mere figment of the imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical effect of hot air making something appear that is not there.

clue.text: Teenager gets drunk, but not on this

definitions.text: Teenager gets drunk, but not on this

indicators.note: something drunk is all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A teenager gets drunk, though not on a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a teen getting drunk would not do it on a caffeine drink from China.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfermented infusion, popular in East Asia, that cannot make anyone tipsy.
